item.title: Sparse qubit operation in a 6×6 quantum dot array
item.description:
Pay dirt new result — Operated 10 hole spin qubits simultaneously in a 6×6 quantum dot array with a shared barrier grid. Reduced crosstalk by 42× via sparse layout and demonstrated coherent spin shuttling across distances up to 5.2SIUnitSymbolMicro.

Grade 0.492 · 2.3σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Alexader S. Ivlev, Harold L. Co, Damien R. Crielaard, Alice Petrillo, Setareh Kazemzadeh, Giordano Scappucci, Menno Veldhorst

Figure

False-colour AFM image of the 6x6 quantum dot array with labelled plunger gates and merged barrier, alongside 2D maps of Spin Evolution Diagrams, g-factor, and coherence times extracted across the array.

Asks

Can extended 2D quantum dot arrays be operated with high-fidelity single- and two-qubit control without a dense wiring bottleneck?

But

30 of 36 dots coherently accessible; fixed global barrier gate voltage; two-qubit CZ fidelities limited to 66.8±6.0%--71.5±2.5% by dephasing and slow shuttling.

Tools

merged-barrier 6x6 quantum dot array · Ge/SiGe heterostructure · bucket-brigade spin shuttling · Spin Evolution Diagrams · EDSR

Abstract

Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires increasing the qubit count while maintaining high performance and connectivity. Semiconductor qubits have demonstrated high-fidelity operation, but growing the system size at sufficient connectivity remains challenging, such that scaling mainly occurred in one spatial direction to preserve access for control lines in the other. Here, we realise an approach that relaxes the requirements on fabrication and demonstrate a 6×6 quantum dot array, defined by a shared barrier gate and individual plunger gates. The quantum dots are tuned through coherent spin shuttling over distances up to 5.2um into a sparse configuration of 10 simultaneously operated qubits, leaving space for shuttling connections. We reduce crosstalk by 42× in this separated regime, enabling high-fidelity simultaneous single-qubit control, while control-Z operations can be implemented through shuttling and plunger-only control. These results promise high-connectivity quantum circuits, enabled by scaling to two-dimensional geometries and exploiting shuttling.

item.title: Proposing one-sided tetrons as topological qubits for Majorana-based quantum computation
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Connecting four topological wires at one end via a trivial superconducting backbone hybridizes inner Majoranas to finite energy (up to 45 μeV), suppressing residual splitting of surviving free-end Majoranas from (E12+E34)/2 down to E13≈5.5 neV (factor of ∼90) and enhancing coherent precession times from 0.7–0.9 ns to ∼0.1 μs.

Grade 0.447 · 1.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Tudor D. Stanescu, Sumanta Tewari

Figure

Parity lifetime of the free-end Majorana pair plotted against the bridge-induced hybridization energy δ of the joined-end pair, demonstrating a 2 to 3 order of magnitude lifetime increase once |δ|≳10 μeV.

Asks

Can residual Majorana wave-function overlap and short parity lifetimes in tetron qubits be suppressed without increasing physical nanowire length or quantum dot size?

Before

Two-sided InAs-Al tetron gave τX=14.5±0.3 μs with fast coherent precession ∼3 ns set by intrawire Majorana splitting E12∼E34∼0.1 μeV.

But

Numerical simulations of clean and disordered 1D/2D models; assumes non-topological superconducting bridge, fixed total parity, and charge noise model on readout quantum dot; does not model full four-arm readout network.

Tools

semiconductor-superconductor hybrid nanowire model · Rashba spin-orbit coupling with Zeeman field · tight-binding BdG simulations · low-energy quantum-dot-coupled master equation

Abstract

One-dimensional SM-SC hybrid nanowires with Rashba spin-orbit coupling and applied Zeeman field can support Majorana zero modes (MZMs) at the ends of the wire. In finite-length systems, residual wave-function overlap between the end modes produces an energy splitting. In a two-sided tetron qubit, composed of a pair of parallel Majorana wires coupled by a trivial SC backbone in the middle, this splitting limits the parity lifetime associated with Majorana pairs involving both wires and the coherence of the qubit, adversely affecting measurement-based braiding and readout operations. Here, we propose a one-sided tetron made of four parallel Majorana wires connected at a common end by an SC backbone. In the topological phase, the free wire ends host four MZMs that define the topological qubit, while the Majoranas localized near the opposite ends hybridize through the backbone and acquire finite energy. To study the basic hybridization mechanism, we consider a simpler two-wire subsystem, i.e., half of a one-sided tetron, which we call a doublon. In a doublon, the backbone, or bridge, strongly hybridizes the two Majorana modes at the connected end and shifts them away from zero energy, while the modes at the free ends form a near-zero energy fermion. We show that the splitting of the surviving MZM pair can fall by about two orders of magnitude compared to the splitting energies in a two-sided tetron, thereby dramatically increasing the parity lifetimes. Thus, the one-sided tetron ensures a suppression of the Majorana overlap comparable to doubling the length of the corresponding two-sided tetron.

item.title: Protecting bosonic codes from ancilla-induced errors with continuous-variable flags
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Dispersively coupling an auxiliary harmonic oscillator mode (continuous-variable flag) to the control ancilla maps continuous ancilla-decay errors into phase-space displacements; heterodyne readout and feedback reduce cat-code parity measurement logical errors by more than three orders of magnitude.

Grade 0.432 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Superconducting Qubits: Current State of Play” · Thomas Décultot, Ronan Gautier, Mazyar Mirrahimi

Figure

Logical error rate of four-component cat-code parity measurement as a function of flag amplitude or heterodyne measurement efficiency, showing over three orders of magnitude error reduction compared to the bare unflagged gate.

Asks

How can continuous errors propagated to a bosonic storage mode by ancilla decay during conditional gates be detected and corrected?

But

Simulations assume realistic circuit-QED parameters; one-flag conditional displacement protocol fails at first order when ancilla excitation occurs, requiring two flags to resolve arbitrary jump histories.

Tools

Continuous-variable flag mode · Dispersive qubit-oscillator coupling · Heterodyne detection and feedback · Echoed conditional displacement (ECD)

Abstract

Bosonic quantum error correction represents a route towards significant hardware overhead reduction for fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, controlling quantum harmonic oscillators that encode the quantum information comes with its own challenges. In many platforms such as superconducting circuits and trapped ions, the bosonic degree of freedom is controlled by an ancillary qubit whose decay during a qubit-oscillator gate propagates to the oscillator as a continuous error. Such errors generally lie beyond the scope of errors that the bosonic code is capable of correcting. We introduce the continuous-variable flag: an auxiliary oscillator coupled to the ancilla whose phase-space position encodes the continuous error corrupting the storage mode. After the gate, a heterodyne measurement of the flag estimates this continuous-variable error and a subsequent feedback control undoes it up to a bosonic code stabilizer. The scheme requires no new ingredients, as the flag is driven by the same dispersive coupling, displacements and rotations that implement the gates it is supposed to protect. We construct sequences protecting conditional rotations to all orders in ancilla decay with one flag, and conditional displacements to first order with one flag and to all orders with two. Simulations with realistic circuit-QED parameters predict more than three orders of magnitude fewer logical errors for the parity measurement of a four-component cat code, and a finite-energy GKP logical lifetime near its noiseless-ancilla bound. By discretizing continuous-variable errors, the flags introduced in this work are a useful tool for any hybrid oscillator-qubit processor, and open the route towards fault-tolerant simulation and computation with bosonic modes.

item.title: Quasiparticle-resolved variational theory of Andreev spin qubits
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Two-quasiparticle (2-QP) configurations supply exactly 50% of the leading spin-dependent Josephson coupling ES at U=0 via coherence with 0-QP states, and dominate ES as Coulomb interaction U increases.

Grade 0.431 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Charge-insensitive qubit design derived from the Cooper pair box” · Teodor Ilivcin, Rok vZitko

Figure

Lead quasiparticle sector probabilities and coherence contributions to the spin coupling coefficient as functions of U/Δ. Panel (b) shows the 02 coherence and 11 sector fractions of the total weak-hybridization spin coupling.

Asks

How do virtual continuum Bogoliubov quasiparticles and Coulomb interactions microscopically determine the spin-dependent and conventional Josephson couplings in Andreev spin qubits?

But

Variational derivation truncated at 2 Bogoliubov quasiparticles; evaluated at particle-hole symmetry δ=0, flat normal-state density of states, and small background tunneling W.

Tools

continuum Bogoliubov quasiparticle variational Ansatz · Anderson impurity model with interlead background hopping · Numerical Renormalization Group (NRG) · Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG)

Abstract

An Andreev spin qubit stores a single unpaired spin, yet its coupling to the superconducting phase can be dominated by coherent virtual quasiparticle pairs. We develop a continuum variational description of the odd-parity doublet in a quantum-dot Josephson junction with Coulomb interaction and spin-dependent background tunneling. Retaining configurations with up to two Bogoliubov quasiparticles provides compact analytical expressions for energies and wavefunctions. We benchmark the results against numerical renormalization group calculations and identify sources of error. We obtain closed-form expressions for the conventional and spin-dependent Josephson couplings. Despite their small probability, two-quasiparticle configurations, through coherence with the zero-quasiparticle component, supply exactly half of the leading spin-dependent Josephson coupling even without Coulomb repulsion and dominate it as the repulsion grows. Spin-orbit-induced spin transfer between the dot and the leads produces a Josephson-current contribution that is common to both qubit states and finite at zero phase bias when the dot and lead Zeeman energies differ. We also map the localization of the virtual quasiparticles and the spin density in the leads. The results connect strongly correlated quantum-dot models to effective Hamiltonians used for Andreev-spin-qubit circuits and clarify how the wavefunction structure determines their couplings.

item.title: Dynamics of quantum measurement via electron transport in quantum dot systems: many-particle wavefunction approach
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Master equations and current noise power spectra derived for quantum point contacts with arbitrary internal quantum dot graph structures coupled to a charge qubit via Coulomb interaction. For cyclic N-dot graphs in the weak tunneling limit, stationary current scales as I(∞)∼Ω2/Γ.

Grade 0.429 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “exchange gates and two-qubit operations in semiconductor double quantum dots” · George Stavisskii, Leonid Fedichkin

Figure

Schematic of a cyclic N-site quantum dot graph coupled to point contact leads, which diagonalizes to level widths Γnk=(Γ/N)cos⁡(2π(n−k)/N) and energies En=2Ωcos⁡(2πn/N).

Asks

How to rigorously describe non-equilibrium electron transport, measurement, and current noise power spectra in point contacts with complex internal graph structures coupled to a charge qubit without phenomenological probes?

But

High voltage bias limit; spin degrees of freedom neglected due to Coulomb blockade; leads treated in wide-band approximation; requires finite relaxation rate Γr>0 to avoid unphysical nonzero noise perturbations as δΓ→0.

Tools

many-particle wavefunction approach · Bardeen transfer Hamiltonian · Laplace transform contour integration · single-particle Bogolyubov transformation · density matrix master equations

Abstract

Measurement of a charge qubit via point contacts with complex internal structures is considered. In this context, a fully formalized derivation of the many-body wave function method is presented, together with the corresponding master equations for point contacts possessing an arbitrary number of internal states. The focus is placed on the current noise power spectrum and its dependence on the qubit dynamics and the point contact parameters.

item.title: Benchmarking exchange-only control of a 48-spin singlet manifold
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Operating across total-spin-zero manifolds up to 48 electron spins yields an effective system-level fidelity loss of ϵF=3.2×10−4 per two-spin exchange.

Figure

Loss in fidelity per exchange ϵF across device subgraphs up to 48 spins (panel a), and decay of XEB fidelity alongside square-root purity versus exchange pulse count for 12 spins (panel b).

Asks

What aggregate system performance can be achieved by benchmarking exchange-only spin systems across their full total-spin-zero Hilbert space?

Before

Errors >10−3 per fundamental two-body operation on competing quantum computing platforms.

But

Lacks well-defined local qubits and native single-spin Pauli gates. Evaluated within the S=0 total angular momentum manifold rather than encoded logical qubits.

Tools

54-quantum-dot silicon chip · cryogenic CMOS controller · cross-entropy benchmarking (XEB) · mirror randomized benchmarking (MRB) · out-of-time-order correlators (OTOC)

Abstract

Exchange-only quantum computing benefits from high fidelity and straightforward control afforded by the exchange interaction. However, independently controllable qubits must be encoded into subsystems of at least three electron spins, restricting computation to only a fraction of the available spin Hilbert space. The remaining states are treated as leakage and used only transiently in gate sequences. By contrast, a quantitative, system-wide measure of exchange-only performance can exploit the full available Hilbert space, including states conventionally treated as leakage. Here, we apply this approach to arrays of up to 48 electron spins, accessing a total-spin-zero Hilbert space with dimension exceeding 2⁴⁰. Measurements of out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) reveal rich scrambling dynamics and demonstrate access to regimes relevant to quantum computational advantage. Using generalized forms of cross-entropy and mirror randomized benchmarking, we also assess the aggregate performance of the full exchange-only system per fundamental two-body interaction: the two-spin exchange. We obtain an effective system-level error of 3 ×10⁻⁴ per exchange, incorporating the complete experimental control sequence and all associated noise sources. This value is up to an order of magnitude lower than those reported from comparable benchmarks on other platforms at the time of writing.

item.arxave:tools: 54-quantum-dot silicon chip · cryogenic CMOS controller · cross-entropy benchmarking (XEB) · mirror randomized benchmarking (MRB) · out-of-time-order correlators (OTOC)
item.arxave:abstract: Exchange-only quantum computing benefits from high fidelity and straightforward control afforded by the exchange interaction. However, independently controllable qubits must be encoded into subsystems of at least three electron spins, restricting computation to only a fraction of the available spin Hilbert space. The remaining states are treated as leakage and used only transiently in gate sequences. By contrast, a quantitative, system-wide measure of exchange-only performance can exploit the full available Hilbert space, including states conventionally treated as leakage. Here, we apply this approach to arrays of up to 48 electron spins, accessing a total-spin-zero Hilbert space with dimension exceeding 2⁴⁰. Measurements of out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) reveal rich scrambling dynamics and demonstrate access to regimes relevant to quantum computational advantage. Using generalized forms of cross-entropy and mirror randomized benchmarking, we also assess the aggregate performance of the full exchange-only system per fundamental two-body interaction: the two-spin exchange. We obtain an effective system-level error of 3 ×10⁻⁴ per exchange, incorporating the complete experimental control sequence and all associated noise sources. This value is up to an order of magnitude lower than those reported from comparable benchmarks on other platforms at the time of writing.

item.title: Quantum dynamics of spin systems using quantum-like resources
item.description:
Worth a look incremental — Constructs quantum-like (QL) gate circuits on complex synchronized networks to prepare wavepackets and simulate transverse-field Ising model time evolution and magnetization, mapping network topology transformations via microscopic coupling, phase coherence, and inter-block coupling metrics.

Grade 0.414 · 1.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “scaling up: crossbar addressing, cryo-CMOS control, qubit interconnects” · Debadrita Saha, Ethan Dickey, William Horvat, Sabre Kais, Gregory D. Scholes

Asks

Can classical complex synchronized networks and quantum-like gates simulate the dynamical time evolution and physical observables of interacting spin systems?

But

Classical network simulation rather than physical hardware implementation; constrained by classical resource scaling and synchronization requirements.

Tools

quantum-like (QL) bits and gates · complex synchronized networks · transverse-field Ising model Hamiltonian simulation · graph connectivity metrics

Abstract

Recent publications have introduced the concept of quantum-like (QL) bits, along with their associated QL-states and QL-gate operations, emerging from the dynamics of complex synchronized networks. The present work builds on this framework to present a simulation of quantum dynamics in spin systems. We focus on the transverse field Ising model, a widely studied Hamiltonian for interacting spin systems. We show how circuits, built using the QL analog of quantum gates, can be used to prepare an arbitrary initial wavepacket and simulate the time evolution of the resulting state for extracting physical observables such as magnetization. Beyond the statevector dynamics, we introduce a set of metrics that characterize how QL-circuit operations transform the underlying graph connections. These metrics quantify the microscopic coupling, phase coherence, and effective inter-block coupling generated by the circuit. These graph-level quantities provide constraints and design targets for potential physical implementations, indicating where interconnection resources, phase control, and effective coupling strength must be engineered in a hardware realization. Overall, this study demonstrates how classical resources can be harnessed to simulate quantum systems and we discuss the advantages and limitations.
